newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies to press ahead with reform voting.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies to press ahead with reform voting.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies will begin voting on a series of amendments to a civil service reform bill Wednesday, but amendments on sensitive points will be probably be left for another date, an official said.
"They will vote on some things today, but nothing polemical," said the official, an aide to government chief whip in the lower house Deputy Benito Gama.
More than 100 amendments to the bill have been presented by opposition and government lawmakers.
Some of the proposals would remove key clauses of the reform and government whips fear they might not muster the 308 votes, equivalent to a three-fifths majority, needed to defeat them.

The government angered many members of the lower house earlier this week when it withdrew its support from a controversial amendment which would have exempted lawmakers from a proposed 10,800 real ($10,188) ceiling on pay and pension.
The government had agreed to the exemption as "the price to pay" for approving the reform bill in the Chamber of Deputies.
The bill was approved for a first time in the lower house last week with 309 votes, just one more than needed.
